name: C Algorithms
listed_description: Collection of common algorithms and data structures.
reason: No numeric comparison anywhere reachable. README.md describes a modular teaching-style collection (copy a .c/.h pair, ISC licence) with no performance claim at all; repo root has doc, src and test only (doc holds Doxygen files, no benchmark), NEWS.md has no speed or benchmark mentions, and issue search for 'benchmark' returns only an invalid PR on test-sortedarray.c. No third-party shootout including libcalg was found.

name: c-capnproto
listed_description: Implementation of the Cap'n Proto serialization protocol.
reason: No numeric comparison anywhere reachable. The repo (archived 2023-11-04, MIT, 69 stars) has no README and no benchmark file (root: compiler, capn.c, capn.h, capn-malloc.c, capn-stream.c, tests); all 7 issues are install, usage and compiler-warning reports, none about speed or msgpack. A web search found only Cap'n Proto C++ comparisons against protobuf, not this C implementation against msgpack or anything else.

name: C-Macro-Collections
listed_description: Generate simple and generic data structures using macros.
reason: Harness but no numbers. The repo has benchmarks/benchmark.c (CMC hashtable and heap timings, no baseline) and benchmarks/comparisons/hashtable (hashmap.c and hashmultimap.c against unorderedmap.cpp, a std::unordered_map with MurmurHash, built with -O3 and timed with hyperfine at COUNT=20000000), but no result numbers appear in the README, the mdBook docs index (searchindex.json has no benchmark, unordered or C++ mentions) or the issues; issue #10 says the examples and benchmarks are outdated. README only has design claims (array-based structures are faster due to caching). Directional only, so no record.

name: cchan
listed_description: Small library for channel constructs for inter-thread communication.
reason: No numeric comparison reachable. repo.hu and the 2010 suckless dev-list announcement were EGRESS_BLOCKED; a web search snippet describes a very small mutex and condition-variable channel library for pthreads and SDL threads with select() planned, and mentions no benchmark. No GitHub repo exists for it (github.com/tembleking/cchan is an unrelated C++17 library). Directional claim at most.

name: ck (Concurrency Kit)
listed_description: Concurrency primitives, safe memory reclamation mechanisms and non-blocking data structures.
reason: No published number against a named baseline reachable. README only says ck_epoch is 'better than or competitive with many state-of-the-art solutions' (directional). The repo has benchmark harnesses (regressions/ck_spinlock/benchmark builds pthread and linux_spinlock binaries beside the ck locks; ck_ring/benchmark/latency.c; ck_hs/benchmark serial.c, apply.c, parallel_bytestring.c) but no checked-in results, and issue searches for benchmark, faster, slower and liburcu find nothing with numbers. concurrencykit.org, the 2012 Linux Plumbers slides, speakerdeck, deepwiki and the Google Groups release notes were EGRESS_BLOCKED; searches for third-party papers or shootouts that include ck found none.
